# v14 = v13.1 + the v12 aggression switches (built Sun 15 Nov, 01:45)

**File:** `v14/bot.py`, SHA-256 `3ec3640e274a2247…`, 94.8 KB.

**Generated by:** scratchpad `make_v14.py` from `v13/bot.py` (v13.1, `26c93325…`, see `../v13/CHANGES.md`).

**The four switches:** the same code that was benchmarked on top of v11.1 as `testbench/out/test_adapt/bots/v11sw_all.py` (+2.7 bb/100 there).

| Switch | What it does |
|---|---|
| `V12_FOLD_BLEND` = 0.5 (B1) | Half of a villain's calling behaviour is modelled as independent of his hand, at his measured continue rate. `FOLD_P` takes the R19–R54 measured values (0.28, 0.50, 0.60, 0.72). |
| `V12_VALUE` (B2) | Overbets from uh 0.80 (was 0.90). Big heads-up bets against measured sticky callers from uh 0.76. |
| `V12_HU_BLUFF` (B3) | Heads-up bluffs when checked to may be up to 1.05 pot. In practice: pot-size flop bluffs, and pot-size in-position turn/river barrels. v13's line rules take precedence: out-of-position turn/river barrels and leads stay ≤ 0.75 pot and ≥ 0.6 pot, and v12's flat 0.45 cap only applies if `V13_LINE_BLUFF` is switched off. |
| `V12_LIGHT3` (B5) | Light 3-bets (ace / pair / suited connector, u ≤ 0.45) against openers measured folding ≥ 55% to 3-bets. |

## Benchmarks (paired, identical deals; bb/100, all-in luck removed)

Adaptive Sunday bench (`duel_ends.py --adaptive`, Table C copies that adapt to our bet frequency and 3-bet us exploitatively):

| Comparison | Deals 201 / 301 / 401 (240 pairs each) | Pooled, 720 pairs | Per opponent |
|---|---|---|---|
| v14 vs v13.1 | +1.2 / +1.1 / +1.1 | **+1.14 ± 0.46, z 2.5** | none negative (+0.06 … +0.26) |
| v14 vs v11sw_all (v11.1 + the same switches) | +1.6 / +0.8 / +1.1 | **+1.18 ± 0.39, z 3.0** | FisherMen +0.85 (z 4.0; v13's 4-bet edge); smallest −0.10 ± 0.15 |
| v13.1 vs v11.1 (for reference) | +3.2 / +2.9 / +2.1 | **+2.75 ± 0.39, z 6.8** | all positive; FisherMen +1.14 |

**Where v14's gain over v13.1 comes from:**
- pots won uncontested: +3.99 ± 0.16;
- chips lost in hands we later fold: −2.28 ± 0.19 (flop bluffs that are called and given up on the turn);
- showdowns: −0.63 ± 0.46.

Other benches (paired, identical deals):

| Test | v14 vs v13.1 | v14 vs v11sw_all |
|---|---|---|
| Static Sunday bench (non-adaptive copies), deals 201 / 301 / 401 | +0.1 / +2.9 / +0.9; pooled **+1.30 ± 0.49, z 2.6** (matcha −0.27 ± 0.16, the only negative opponent; it is +0.20 on the adaptive bench) | +1.3 / +0.2 / +1.0; pooled **+0.85 ± 0.36, z 2.3** |
| `simreal`: the 36 real Saturday line-ups, adaptive copies | +1.66 ± 1.12 | +2.64 ± 0.84 |
| `simreal`, static copies | +0.40 ± 1.20 | |
| Random 7-seat tables (6 opponents drawn from the whole field), adaptive | **+4.0 ± 1.2, z 3.4** | |

**Verdict:** v14 beats v13.1 on every test: significant on both pooled Sunday benches and on random tables, and positive on both real-line-up replays.

**Fresh-deal confirmation (04:10), guarding against selection bias.** A sister candidate (v15) failed exactly this check.

| Test | v14 vs v13.1 |
|---|---|
| Adaptive bench, 6 FRESH deal sets 801–1301 | +0.7 / −2.1 / +0.9 / +1.4 / +2.6 / +1.4; pooled **+0.82 ± 0.36, z 2.3**. No negative opponent (The Market Makers +0.38, z 2.8). |
| Adaptive bench, all 9 sets | **+0.93 ± 0.28, z 3.3** |
| Static bench, all 6 sets (3 fresh: −0.8 / +1.0 / +1.6) | **+0.96 ± 0.36, z 2.7** |

**Known cost:** v14 loses more at showdown (−1.45 ± 0.36 on the fresh sets). That is the price of its bigger value bets and bluffs, and it is outweighed by +4.08 in pots won uncontested.

## Independent code review (Sun 02:15): **ship**

- **No crash, illegality or timing defect.** With all four switches off, v14 makes the same decision as v13.1 at every one of the 46,342 real decision points (R19–R54), raise sizes included.
- **Low-severity model notes, all also present in the benchmarked v11sw_all:**
  1. The blend makes a villain's strongest hands fold 14–36% in the model. That inflates our equity-when-called for big bets: 123 extra heavy overbets in the replay. B1 alone measured +0.32 ± 0.53 on the v11.1 bench. Being tested as `v14b0`.
  2. The raise risk is not rescaled for the blend. Minor.
  3. Pot-size flop bluffs are now also allowed out of position (233 replay decisions), where the field folds only 43–50%. Being tested as `v15e` / `v15c`.
  4. `sticky_` can fire on two observed calls. One extra big bet in 36 rounds.
- Python 3.11 / 3.13 smoke tests are clean. Fuzz: 27,344 decisions (normal and 40× slow clock), 0 exceptions, 0 fallbacks, 0 illegal actions.
